Born in [[London]] to Nigerian parents, Azubuike moved to the United States as a child. He was raised in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]], where he became a standout player at [[Victory Christian School (Tulsa, Oklahoma)|Victory Christian High School]], and was eventually recruited to play for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] of the [[University of Kentucky]]. After finishing his junior season in college, Azubuike declared himself eligible for the [[2005 NBA draft]], eventually going undrafted that year. Azubuike then played for the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the NBA Development League, leading the league in scoring during the 2006–07 season and eventually being called up to play for the [[Golden State Warriors]]. ==Early life== Azubuike was born in [[London]], England, to Nigerian parents Kenneth and Chi Azubuike.{{cite web |last1=Strain |first1=Mike |title=Azubuike destined for greatness All the hoopla not just hype - this kid can play |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/article/2747658/azubuike-destined-for-greatness-all-the-hoopla-not-just-hype-this-kid-can-play |website=The Oklahoman |access-date=April 20, 2021 |date=July 8, 2001}} His parents were doctors and had moved to London for work. Azubuike relocated with his family to [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]], in 1989 when his father was offered a fellowship at [[Medical facilities in Tulsa#Saint Francis Health System|Saint Francis Hospital]]; his family became American citizens. Playing for [[Victory Christian School (Tulsa, Oklahoma)|Victory Christian High School]], Azubuike led his team to the state title as a sophomore. He eventually became an All-State selection, averaging 39.1 points and 13.3 rebounds and leading his team to the Class 4A State Championship Game as a senior. He was the top scorer in the state of Oklahoma during his last three seasons of high school, averaging 28.5 points as a sophomore and 38.7 points as a junior. Azubuike finished his prep career with 3,530 points, 89 points short of the all-time state scoring mark. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Scout.com]], Azubuike was listed as the No. 8 small forward and the No. 34 player in the nation in 2002.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/11381n-kelenna-azubuike Kelenna Azubuike Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Playing under coach [[Tubby Smith]], Azubuike said that the biggest improvement to his game at Kentucky was the ability to create offense through intense defense.{{cite web|last=Maloney|first=Mark|url=http://www.kentucky.com/818/story/612402.html|title=Ex-Cat Azubuike earning respect of NBA peers : KentuckySports.com|publisher=KentuckySports.com|access-date=19 July 2009}} As a junior, Azubuike was named to the All-SEC Second Team by the [[Associated Press]] and the league's coaches after leading the team and ranking tenth in the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] in points per game, averaging 14.7 overall. Azubuike was named to the 2005 SEC All-Tournament Team after averaging 18.0 points in three contests. During his time with the organization, Azubuike helped the Wildcats to earn two Southeastern Conference titles, two SEC Tournament titles, and two NCAA [[Elite Eight]] appearances. Azubuike averaged 10.0 points and 3.7 rebounds in 97 career games at the University of Kentucky, shooting a 48.5% field goal average for his college career. While attending the [[University of Kentucky]], Azubuike majored in [[business marketing]]. ==Professional career== ===Fort Worth Flyers (2005–2007)=== In April 2005, Azubuike announced his plans to enter the draft after his junior year, signing with agent Joel Bell and ending his college eligibility.{{cite magazine|title=SI.com – NCAA Basketball – UK's Morris remains in draft as deadline passes – Tuesday June 21, 2005|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=21 June 2005|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2005/basketball/ncaa/06/21/bc.bkc.kentucky.morris.ap|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025034443/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2005/basketball/ncaa/06/21/bc.bkc.kentucky.morris.ap/|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 October 2012|access-date=16 July 2009}} In the 2005–06 season, Azubuike averaged 12.6 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assists in forty-one games with the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the NBA's [[NBA Development League|Developmental League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/azubuike-waived-102406.shtml|title=InsideHoops.com – Kelenna Azubuike released by Houston Rockets|publisher=[[Inside Hoops]]|access-date=2 January 2007}} Azubuike played with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the 2006 Toshiba Vegas Summer League, where he averaged 16.4 points and finished tied at tenth in the league in scoring. In August 2006, Azubuike was signed by the [[Houston Rockets]] as a free agent, but eventually waived by October. Playing for Fort Worth of the Development League again, Azubuike averaged 5.0 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.17 steals, and a league-best 26.0 points in 37.7 minutes per contest, shooting 51.4% from the field and 48.5% from three-point range over twelve games.{{cite news|title=WARRIORS: Warriors Sign Kelenna Azubuike to Contract|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Kelenna_Azubuike_Signing_Release.html|access-date=28 July 2009}} ===Golden State Warriors (2007–2010)=== [[File:Kelenna Azubuike shoots free throw at Suns at Warriors 3-15-09 1.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Azubuike with the Golden State Warriors in 2009]] After going undrafted, Azubuike was signed by the [[Golden State Warriors]] on 2 January 2007. He was the first [[Gatorade]] Call-Up of the 2006–07 NBA Development League season, and the 49th player overall to be called up to the NBA since the D-League began play in November 2001. During his second season with Golden State, Azubuike expressed an interest in playing for the [[Great Britain|British]] team during the build-up to the [[2012 Summer Olympics|2012 London Olympic Games]], but was denied British citizenship under the [[British Nationality Act 1981|1981 British Nationality Act]].{{cite news|title=Blow for Britain as London-born Kelenna Azubuike is denied passport – Times Online|last=Whittell|first=Ian|newspaper=[[The Times]]|date=31 December 2007|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/more_sport/us_sport/article3111497.ece|access-date=31 December 2007}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} He was also eligible to play for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national team]].{{cite web |last1=Rushworth |first1=Simon |title=Kelenna spoilt for choice |url=https://www.express.co.uk/sport/othersport/4100/Kelenna-spoilt-for-choice |website=Express |access-date=January 23, 2023 |date=April 11, 2007}} On 17 July 2008, Azubuike signed an offer sheet with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for a three-year deal worth $9 million, with Golden State having seven days to match the offer.{{cite news|title=Sources: Clips sign swingman Azubuike to three-year offer sheet – NBA – ESPN|last=Stein|first=Marc|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=18 July 2008|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3494107|access-date=18 July 2008}} In the final hour, Golden State matched the offer made by the Clippers on 24 July 2008, allowing Azubuike to remain a Warrior.{{cite news|title=Warriors keep Azubuike, match Clippers' offer – NBA – ESPN|publisher=ESPN|date=24 July 2008|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3503935|access-date=24 July 2008}} On 17 November 2009, it was announced that Azubuike would miss the rest of the 2009–10 season after tearing his right patellar tendon in a game at the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].Marcus Thompson II. "[http://www.mercurynews.com/warriors-headlines/ci_13804386 Warriors' Kelenna Azubuike out for the season, C.J. Watson has swine flu]". ''San Jose Mercury News''. 17 November 2009. Retrieved on 17 November 2009. On 9 July 2010, Azubuike was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] along with [[Anthony Randolph]], [[Ronny Turiaf]] and a future second-round pick in a [[sign and trade]] deal for [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/randolph_acquired070910.html|title=Knicks Acquire Randolph, Azubuike & Turiaf|date=9 July 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=9 July 2010}} Azubuike never played in a game for the Knicks. He was waived by the Knicks on 28 February 2011.[http://www.nba.com/2011/news/03/01/knicks.azubuike.ap/index.html Knicks waive guard Kelenna Azubuike] ===Dallas Mavericks (2012)=== On 23 March 2012, Azubuike was signed by the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. ===Texas Legends (2012)=== As part of his comeback, he was assigned to the Mavericks' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]].[https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/7727156/kelenna-azubuike-signs-dallas-mavericks Kelenna Azubuike to Mavericks] On 9 April 2012, he was recalled by the Mavericks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4687797/kaleena-azubuike-gets-call-to-replace-lamar-odom|title=Kelenna Azubuike gets call to replace Lamar Odom|date=9 April 2012|work=[[ESPN]]}} On 20 April 2012, Azubuike played in his first NBA game since 14 November 2009, against the Golden State Warriors.{{cite web|url=http://www.allkyhoops.com/2012/04/kelenna-azubuike-sees-first-nba-action.html|title=Azubike plays in first NBA game in three seasons|date=21 April 2012|work=allkyhoops.com}} On 28 June 2012, during the [[2012 NBA draft]], Azubuike was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4690229/mavs-add-kelenna-azuibuike-to-trade Mavs add Kelenna Azuibuike to trade] He was waived by the Cavaliers on 14 October 2012.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/azubuike-waivers-121013 Cavaliers Waive Keleena Azubuike] ==Broadcasting career== In the summer of 2015, Azubuike attended the [[Sportscaster U.]] program at [[Syracuse University]] sponsored by the [[National Basketball Players Association|NBPA]], training for a career in broadcasting.{{cite web |url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article44612136.html |title=UK basketball notebook: Ex-Cats Azubuike, Mohammed take crash course in broadcasting |work=Kentucky Sports |date=15 July 2015}} Since then, he has been assigned to announce 11 of the 19 NBA D-League games produced by NBA TV in 2016.{{cite web |url=http://dleaguedigest.com/2016/01/03/nba-d-league-alum-kelenna-azubuike-heading-broadcast-booth-d-league-showcase/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412191849/http://dleaguedigest.com/2016/01/03/nba-d-league-alum-kelenna-azubuike-heading-broadcast-booth-d-league-showcase/ |url-status=usurped |date=7 January 2016 |work=dleague.nba.com |access-date=30 March 2016 |archive-date=27 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160327050251/http://dleague.nba.com/news/espnu-televise-nba-dleague-games-2016-season-schedule/ |url-status=dead }} He joined [[NBC Sports Bay Area]] in 2015, covering Warriors games as a studio analyst for the pregame, halftime, and postgame shows. Beginning in 2019, he became the television analyst alongside [[Bob Fitzgerald]], replacing [[Jim Barnett (basketball)|Jim Barnett]], who had been the color analyst for the last 34 seasons and is now the color analyst on [[KGMZ-FM|KGMZ-FM's 95.7 The Game]]. Azubuike has also worked as an analyst for the NBA on ESPN Radio since 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/kelenna-azubuike-be-warriors-tv-game-analyst-jim-barnett-radio | first=Monte |last=Poole |title=Kelenna Azubuike to be Warriors TV game analyst; Jim Barnett to radio | access-date=26 July 2019| date=26 July 2019}} ==Personal life== In October 2022, Azubuike married Rona in an intimate ceremony after four years of dating. A year later, the couple had a grand multicultural wedding, where they celebrated with their family and friends. Azubuike has three siblings: Nonzo, Nesochi and Adaeze. He is a Christian music fan and enjoys creating his own music. During the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Azubuike made an appearance on [[San Francisco Bay Area|Bay Area]] hip hop station [[KMEL]] and conducted an interview while the station played music which he personally produced. Azubuike is a [[Christians|Christian]].{{cite web |url=http://www.breathecast.com/articles/former-nba-star-kelenna-azubuike-shares-details-on-new-faith-based-film-midrange-and-being-a-christian-among-pro-athletes-16358/ |title=Former NBA Star Kelenna Azubuike Shares Details on New Faith Based Film 'Midrange' and Being a Christian Among Pro-Athletes (VIDEO INTERVIEW) |last1=Sarachik |first1=Justin |date=13 June 2014 |website=Breathecast |access-date=6 February 2015}} Azubuike has been involved with many humanitarian causes during his time in the NBA. Azubuike accepted a personal invitation from [[Jakaya Kikwete]], the President of [[Tanzania]], to take part in [[Leon Sullivan#Leon H. Sullivan Summit|Leon H. Sullivan Summit VIII]], a five-day [[Convention (meeting)|convention]] held from 2 to 6 June 2008 in [[Arusha]], Tanzania. The convention brought together many of the world's political and business leaders to focus attention and resources on Africa's economic and social development.{{cite news|title=WARRIORS: Kelenna Azubuike: On A Mission To Tanzania|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Kelenna_Tanzania.html|access-date=20 July 2009}} Azubuike is also the co-founder of The Athletes' Corner, which is a nonprofit organization working with professional athletes to create faith-based and family-focused media content. The Golden State Warriors, Kaiser Permanente, and The Athletes' Corner have launched the 'Swishes for Dishes' initiative, a program donating meals to Bay Area food banks for each point scored. The initiative has resulted in the donation of over 5.4 million meals. Key aspects of the partnership include a donation of 100 meals for every point scored during the 2024–26 season and a focus on addressing food insecurity and promoting health and wellness in local communities. The program has had a total impact of providing millions of meals to families in need across the Bay Area.https://theathletescorner.org The Athletes’ Corner ==NBA career statistics== ===Regular
